**1. Outside view.**
Weekly changes over the last 10 releases: -0.2, +1.1, -1.2, -0.4, -1.1, -1.5, +1.9, -0.9, -1.5. Mean drift ≈ -0.42/week, SD of weekly change ≈ 1.15. The series has trended steadily downward from about -9.4 in early July to -13.2 on Sept 4, i.e. roughly -0.4 pts/week, with occasional 1–2 pt bounces (Aug 21 snapped back +1.9 after a -12.7 reading). Naive extrapolation: last value plus drift ≈ -13.6. But the Aug 14 → Aug 21 episode shows that a fresh "new low" print is often partly overshoot, so an equally plausible naive anchor is roughly the last value unchanged or modestly reverted (-12.8 to -13.2).

**2. Inside view.**
National Civiqs net has been pinned at about -24 through all of August (Aug 19 and Aug 27 both -24), i.e. the topline is flat while the male subgroup has been drifting down — suggesting some of the male decline is compositional/model noise rather than a broad new shock. Other trackers (Reuters/Ipsos stuck at 33% for three straight weeks) also show a flat-to-slightly-soft environment, not an accelerating collapse. No identifiable discrete event in the Sept 4–11 window (economy stories, midterm framing) worth more than a few tenths. So: continuation of secular drift worth about -0.3; partial mean reversion off a fresh low worth about +0.3. Net ≈ 0.

**3. Pre-mortem.**
Most likely way I'm badly wrong: the -13.2 print was the leading edge of a genuine step-down (economic news / a specific controversy hitting male voters), and Friday shows -15 or worse; alternatively it was an overshoot and the model snaps back to -11.5 as it did on Aug 21. Both failure modes are symmetric-ish around my center, which argues for keeping the mean near -13.2 rather than fully extrapolating the trend, and for a wide SD that accommodates a ~2 pt bounce.

**4. Calibrate.**
Weekly move SD ≈ 1.15; adding a bit of uncertainty about whether the trend or reversion dominates, an SD of ~1.2 puts roughly two-thirds of outcomes in [-14.4, -12.0], which matches observed week-to-week behavior (most moves under 1.5, occasional ~1.9).
